title: 30-Year Treasury Bond auction (December reopening) — the only leg of the block that prices AFTER the FOMC, and it lands on CPI morning
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, PDF CreationDate 2026-08-04), FlateDecode streams inflated PER PAGE and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates. The page-3 row reads verbatim `30-Year BOND / R / Thursday, December 03, 2026 / Thursday, December 10, 2026 / Tuesday, December 15, 2026` — the `R` marks a REOPENING. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-03 coupon announcement
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-3y-note-2026-12-07 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), reading the same schedule PDF that dates that event. Filed because the calendar tracks treasury-30y-bond-2026-09-10, -10-08 and -11-12 as first-class medium-impact entries and then stops — there is no canonical or proposed December 30-Year anywhere, and the November sibling (treasury-3y-note-2026-11-09) explicitly named this leg as discovered-but-not-filed so that a later sweep could file it. This is that sweep. WHY IT DESERVES ITS OWN LEDGER RATHER THAN A LINE IN THE 3-YEAR'S, and it is the sharpest of the three legs: it is the ONLY coupon auction in the December block that stops AFTER the FOMC decision (`fomc-2026-12-09`, tracked) rather than before it — D+1 — and it stops on the SAME MORNING as the November CPI print (`cpi-2026-12-10`, tracked, `high`). So a 30-Year bidder at 1:00pm ET on 12-10 has both the policy decision and the inflation print in hand, where the 3-Year bidder on 12-07 has neither. That makes the block a three-point natural experiment on the same day's supply — D-2, D-1, D+1 — and the long end is where term premium, not the policy path, does the work, which is the standing distinction the existing 30-Year ledgers draw against the 3-Year ones. A REOPENING: the security and its CUSIP already exist, so a when-issued level is quotable well before the auction. EXPECTED SIZE, per the grid rather than any published document: $25B, the standing 30-Year size behind Treasury's 'at least the next several quarters' language; the number becomes published on 2026-12-03 and the size decision belonged to the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding statement, which also carried the expiry of the doubled $4B/op long-end buyback program the November 30-Year ledger tracks. CORRIDOR: it prices the day before the government-funding deadline / CR expiry (12-11) and settles 12-15. DISCOVERED IN THE SAME SWEEP AND FILED SEPARATELY: `treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-03` and `treasury-10y-note-2026-12-08`. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
